$comment: MACHINE-READABLE EXIT CRITERIA for ADR-0042 (vinext + bun --compile --bytecode as the default runtime).
Why this file exists: ADR-0042's phases were prose, so 'has Phase 1 passed?' was a judgement call
re-derived by whoever asked. Every criterion below is a PREDICATE over a MEASURED value.
`measured: null` means nobody has run it — which is a distinct state from measured-and-failing,
and conflating those two is how a phase advances on optimism.
RULE: a value may be written here only with a `source` that names a run ID or a repo path.
`scripts/verify-phase-gates.mjs` fails on a measured value with no source, so a number cannot
title: vinext + bun --compile --bytecode as the default runtime
status: Accepted 2026-08-04 (founder). Delivery phased; the default flip lands at Phase 5.

$comment: ADR-0036's five re-open conditions plus ADR-0042's sixth. A benchmark run that fails ANY of
these is inadmissible as evidence for a phase gate — not 'weaker evidence', inadmissible.
Run 24 is the worked example: it showed a 4.5x win and was withdrawn, because arms were
sequential and the signal turned out to be mode mixture rather than the build target.

conditions.text: same application on both arms, asserted by image digest, not inspection
the requested endpoint recorded in the run's own write-up
build-flag provenance tied to the deployed digest (a build label, not forensics)
results reported per sitting and stratified by mode, never pooled
the vinext arm's binary is SHOWN to contain the application, or the run is labelled shell-only
conditions.why: Consequence 11 — beta.4 serves from binary + dist/ + node_modules/, and the application is not in the binary. A separation result on an artifact whose bytecode coverage is uncharacterised can neither confirm nor refute the objective.

phases.name: bridge proof
phases.status_note: Qualified DONE: the migration landed, but P0-2 is measured FALSE and stays open — vinext beta.4 is not self-contained (it serves from binary + dist/ + node_modules/, with the application NOT in the binary), so the self-containment claim the phase was closed on does not hold on the current toolchain. Recorded rather than reclassified: the phase is genuinely done except for this residual, and forcing it to read DONE or NOT_STARTED would misstate it in one direction or the other.

criteria.text: NO-GO trigger did not fire
self-containment reproduced on CURRENT vinext (beta.4 + Vite 8), not the ^0.0.19 pin
criteria.note: Answered in the negative in the sense that matters: beta.4 serves from binary + dist/ + node_modules/ and the application is NOT in the binary. An earlier draft claimed beta.4 IS self-contained; that was wrong and is corrected, not softened.

criteria.text: clean-directory self-containment RE-VERIFIED under the container rule
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-08, examples/bun-exec on vinext 1.0.0-beta.4 / bun 1.3.5; alpine:3.22 container, strace -ff -e trace=file, as-shipped image (binary + .output/public only)
criteria.note: RE-VERIFIED under the container rule on beta.4: the as-shipped image copies ONLY the binary and .output/public — no dist/, no node_modules/ — and serves HTTP 200 with a real SSR render. Previously UNMEASURED and load-bearing for the whole ADR.

phases.name: artifact provenance
phases.why_gates_phase_1: Phase 1's exit is distribution separation. On an artifact whose bytecode coverage is uncharacterised, a win would be attributed to bytecode that mostly is not there and a loss blamed on a shape nobody intends to ship.

criteria.text: --bytecode verified by binary extraction on the cross-compiled musl target
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-08/09, examples/bun-exec, vinext 1.0.0-beta.4 / bun 1.3.5, target bun-linux-arm64-musl
criteria.method: ADR-0036 Run 26's method — extract from the deployed digest, fingerprint against version-matched controls
criteria.note: CAVEAT, stated rather than glossed: extracted from a LOCALLY BUILT image, not a registry-pulled digest. The method is the one the ADR specifies and the control is version-matched; the provenance chain is one link shorter than "the deployed digest". Closing that link needs a published image.

evidence.method: extract the binary from the built image, fingerprint against a version-matched control built from the SAME input and target differing only in --bytecode
evidence.reading: both arms share an identical 92,017,848-byte Bun runtime prefix; only the appended payload differs. The control payload is 100% printable with zero nulls — minified JS source. The bytecode payload is 9.46x larger, 30.1% printable, one third nulls — a binary blob. Source survives in BOTH (the string LISTENING appears in each), so --bytecode ADDS bytecode rather than replacing source.

criteria.text: bytecode coverage on the cold first request
criteria.unit: fraction of modules served from the binary vs disk
criteria.target_note: No threshold set — this measurement EXISTS to convert 'the app isn't bytecode' from qualitative to a number, and to answer whether shell-only bytecode is most of the win or none of it. A threshold before the first measurement would be invented, not derived.
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-08, examples/bun-exec on vinext 1.0.0-beta.4 / bun 1.3.5; alpine:3.22 container, strace -ff -e trace=file, as-shipped image (binary + .output/public only)

evidence.ssr_verified: body contains real Next HTML with modulepreload, not an error page
evidence.non_vacuity_control: the tracer DOES see app file IO — /app/.output/public/_next/static/chunks/index-D73AVhRX.js appears when that asset is explicitly requested, and /app/server appears. A first attempt reported 0 with NO control and captured only 19 openat lines; that zero was a tracing gap, not an absence, and was discarded.
evidence.only_disk_js_read: the browser chunk explicitly requested — not a server module

criteria.note: CONTRADICTS the premise recorded in Consequence 11 / #658 FOR THIS BUILD SHAPE. The app IS in the binary on the .output/server compile path: zero server modules load from disk. #658 measured the dist/standalone shape, which build.sh does not use. Both shapes exist on beta.4, so the two results are compatible and the ADR text is under-specified rather than wrong.

criteria.text: confirm from a knext-owned entry that the STANDALONE shape also fails to embed the app
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-08/09, examples/bun-exec, vinext 1.0.0-beta.4 / bun 1.3.5, target bun-linux-arm64-musl
criteria.note: STILL UNMEASURED, and the reason is a finding: on this config beta.4 emits NO standalone server at all. `dist/` contains only `dist/server/BUILD_ID` — 4 KB, no server.js. So the standalone shape cannot be confirmed to fail-to-embed here, because it is not produced here. #658 measured a shape this app does not build. Answering P3d-3 requires the config that emits dist/standalone, which is not examples/bun-exec.

criteria.text: is bytecode most of the win, or none of it? (the question P3d-2 exists to answer)
criteria.unit: cold-start improvement, bytecode arm vs same binary without --bytecode
criteria.target_note: No threshold — this is the diagnostic P3d-2 was specified to inform, not a pass/fail gate.
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-09, examples/bun-exec, vinext 1.0.0-beta.4 / bun 1.3.5, bun-linux-arm64-musl, alpine:3.22 containers on local Docker (arm64)

evidence.design: ABBA interleaved, 15 blocks -> 30 paired comparisons; timing taken INSIDE the container from process spawn to first HTTP 200, so host port-mapping is not in the measurement
evidence.axis: --bytecode ON vs OFF. Same app, same target, same input, binaries differing only in that flag.
evidence.separation_note: Ranges OVERLAP (bytecode max 127 > control min 85), driven by outliers above each arm's p75. By ADR-0036's literal bar — separation, not a median difference with overlapping ranges — this does NOT clear it. The 30/0 sign split is nonetheless far stronger than Run 26's 7/5, and the paired design controls for sitting effects.

criteria.note: ANSWERS 3(d)'s stated purpose: bytecode is NOT 'none of the win' — it is ~33% of cold boot on this app. NOT Phase 1 evidence and must not be read as such: Phase 1's axis is node+turbopack vs bun+vinext-compiled; this is bytecode-on vs bytecode-off within one arm. Also LOCAL Docker on arm64, not the OKE cluster, so it fails admissibility for a Phase 1 claim regardless of axis.

evidence.note: Warm baselines indistinguishable between arms, which is what makes the cold delta attributable to the pull.

preconditions.text: the ~10.5 s slow-mode tail is controlled; while it fires, no end-to-end number from that cluster is admissible
preconditions.note: Run 25 measured the same service, digest and probe one day later and saw the slow mode ZERO times — so the base rate MOVES BETWEEN SITTINGS. A single clean sitting therefore does not establish control.

criteria.text: a run satisfying all six admissibility conditions
criteria.source: sitting s-20260811-abba, 2026-08-10/11, context-ckmva7v7zvq, 24 interleaved cold samples
criteria.note: SATISFIED. A1 proven by label equality (app-159989384ca3275f on both arms, images differing by build target); A2/A4 recorded by the harness from the deployed digests; A3 by abba.sh (A B B A blocks, one cold sample per invocation); A5 single sitting, stratified below; A6 measured at P3d-2 (34/34 modules embedded).

attempt.resolver_built: benchmarks/scale-to-zero-oke/image-label-cluster.sh — cluster-side, uses the same ocir-secret the workload pulls with. WORKS: read the image config in-cluster and correctly reported label absence.
attempt.blocker_1_deployed_images_are_unstamped: the deployed p1b-bunexec image has NO LABELS AT ALL (empty .config.Labels, dumped in-cluster). A1 and A4 both depend on labels these images do not carry, so no resolver can make them admissible.
attempt.blocker_2_push_path: docker-credential-osxkeychain HANGS (exit 124 at a 15s bound) for me-abudhabi-1.ocir.io. The registry itself is fine — TCP 443 connects in 701ms and GET /v2/ returns HTTP 401 with a valid Bearer challenge in 639ms. Host credential-agent problem, needs an interactive unlock.
attempt.blocker_3_node_arm_has_no_recipe: the CONTROL arm (p1b-node) has no committed build recipe anywhere in the repo — only examples/bun-exec/build.sh exists. A1 asks that sameness be ASSERTED, not inspected; that assertion cannot be reconstructed for an arm whose build is not in the tree.
attempt.rebuilt_locally: the bun-exec arm WAS rebuilt with all four provenance labels (dev.knext.app.id=bun-exec-9943c605d3d0c4d0, build.command, build.target, build.bun-version), linux/amd64 matching the cluster nodes, and the labels verified on the local image. Only the push is blocked.

criteria.text: distribution separation — NOT a median difference with overlapping ranges
criteria.source: sitting s-20260811-abba, 24 interleaved cold samples (12/arm), OKE context-ckmva7v7zvq

evidence.pooled_reading: looks like a 4.12 s win for bun — and it is NOT one
evidence.stratified_reading: in fast mode the arms are indistinguishable, with bun marginally SLOWER
evidence.conclusion: The entire pooled delta is MODE MIXTURE, not build target. The bimodal ~10-11 s slow mode fired 33% for bun and 50% for node; pooling those makes bun look 4 s faster while fast-mode medians differ by 90 ms in node's favour. This is Run 24's defect reproduced exactly — which is why A5 requires stratification, and why the pooled figure must not be quoted.

superseded_evidence.why: arms were sequential; the apparent 4.5x win was an artifact of WHEN each arm ran, not what it was. Its provisional ~470 ms fast-mode advantage did not reproduce — the sign reversed. Kept here rather than deleted, because the retracted number is the reason condition A3 exists.

criteria.note: PHASE 1 EXIT NOT MET, on an ADMISSIBLE run — all six conditions satisfied. The local 5.12x separation (P1-2-local) does NOT reproduce on the cluster: it measured SERVER BOOT, where the build target dominates, while OKE cold start is dominated by the bimodal slow mode, image pull and scheduling, in which the boot advantage is invisible. The slow-mode incidence difference (4/12 vs 6/12) is not significant at n=12 and must not be read as an effect.

criteria.text: LOCAL proxy for P1-2: does the build-target axis show distribution separation at all?
criteria.source: measured 2026-08-10, examples/bun-exec, both arms native linux/arm64, alpine containers on local Docker; ABBA interleaved, 12 blocks -> 24 paired comparisons; timed INSIDE the container from process spawn to first HTTP 200

evidence.separation_proof: bun max 116 < node min 280 — the ranges do not touch, which is the shape ADR-0036 asks for and which Run 26 (7/5 split, ranges overlapping end to end) did not have
evidence.same_app: app-159989384ca3275f on BOTH arms, from the shared app-id.sh
evidence.same_arch: both native arm64 — a first attempt compared arm64 bun against EMULATED amd64 node and read 208ms vs 1182ms; that comparison was discarded, not reported

criteria.note: NOT Phase 1 clearance and must not be read as it. Phase 1 requires the CLUSTER and all six admissibility conditions; this is local Docker, so A2/A4/A5 are not established and the venue is wrong. What it does establish is that the axis HAS a separable signal — which Run 26 could not show and which was the open question. SCALE IT HONESTLY for platform cold start: 241 ms saved against an OKE image pull that alone costs a measured 2293 ms median (#471), plus scheduling and Knative activation. Real, and roughly a tenth of the cold-start budget — not the dominant term.

criteria.text: per-PR compat-smoke covers the vinext BUILD axis
criteria.note: compat-smoke resolves its server as .next/standalone/.../server.js, so it is bound to Next standalone and does not cover vinext at all. It runs a Node+Bun matrix — the RUNTIME axis — which must not be mistaken for coverage of the BUILD flip. Both lanes boot the same standalone server.js.

blast_radius.consequence: Under a vinext default there is no standalone/server.js, so at Phase 5 those ten rows keep their green while losing red-on-fail backing ON THE DEFAULT PATH — the 'capability behind a check that skips rather than fails' hole workflow.md names as trigger-class.
